Description: The unique feature ID for the record. This field name is generated automatically when the shapefile was created.
The type of feature associated for the record. In this case all of the records are considered to points.
The unique ID of the object (point), for each record.

Unique ID of the school or hostel. A unique id was applied to each school/hostel listed Common Experience Payment of the Indian Residential School Settlement Agreement. Residential schools and hostels not included as part of the IRSSA agreement are also included, although the list isn't exhaustive. This version of the data doesn't include provincially run residential schools, nor does it include schools in Newfoundland and Labrador. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

Unique ID of the school/hostel location. If the school/hostel moved to another property it is considered to be a unique location. If a new school building was constructed on the same property, it isn't considered to be a new location. This code contains the school number followed by the location number. For example, Lejac (41) had two locations, Stuart Lake (411) and Fraser Lake (412).  This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

ID of an related (associated) school/hostel location. Some schools/hostels when they moved formally changed the name and/or ownership. For example, Lac La Biche school closed in 1898, and the staff/students were moved to the first location of Blue Quills School, which was near Saddle Lake. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

Primary authority name of the residential school or hostel used by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation. The name was adapted and based on the Independent Assessment Process and Common Experience Payment Lists. This field was generated by the NCTR.

The earliest operating year of the school or hostel that is officially recognized by the Indian Residential School Residential School Settlement Agreement. This field and data were generated by the NCTR.
The last operating year of the school that is officially recognized by the Indian Residential School Settlement Agreement. This field was generated by the NCTR.

The name of school or hostel location. Many residential schools had more than one location throughout their history. In that case, the name of the school name is provided with the location name in brackets. For example, Portage La Prairie (First Location) and Portage La Prairie (Second Location).  When there is the same name for multiple schools a dash (-) symbol is used to distinguish the schools from each other. For example, St. Michael's - Alert Bay and St. Michael's - Duck Lake. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.
Known alternate names of the school or hostel at that location. This was derived from historical documents and the IAP and CEP lists. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

The year that the school or hostel location opened. The dates were derived from documents provided by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, Church archives and Library Archives Canada. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

The year that the school or hostel location closed. The dates were derived from documents provided by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, Church archives and Library Archives Canada. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

The latitude coordinate of school/hostel location. The latitude coordinate is provided in decimal degrees. This field can be used with the longitude to map the location. This field was generated by the NCTR and defined by Rosa Orlandini.

The longitude coordinates of school/hostel location. The longitude coordinate is provided in decimal degrees. This field can be used with the latitude coordinate to map the location. This field was generated by the NCTR

The individual or group cited for determining the location of the school or hostel. The coordinates are placed, whenever possible on the site of the main school/hostel building at the location. Hite, refers to Morgan Hite (Residential School Atlas), NCTR (National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation), Orlandini (Rosa Orlandini), RSIM (Residential School Interactive Map). This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

Description of the geographical coordinates of the school location. It describes where the main school building or hostel is situated, as well as other key features on the site. For some sites the location of previous buildings on the site are indicated. In this file, the text in the field is limited by 255 characters, so for some records, the user would have to use the IRS_locdescrip.csv file for a complete description of the location. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

The type of school location. "School Location" indicates that it is the location of the Residential School. "Hostel Location" indicates the location of the student hostel associated with a day school. "Hostel and School Location" indicates that the day school and the hostel were on the same property/site. "Mission and School Location" indicates that the mission and the school are on the same site, and the exact location of the school is unknown. "Community Location" indicates the geographical coordinates are for the community, and the precise location of the school/hostel is unknown. This field was created by NCTR and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

The precision of the geographical coordinates for the school/hostel location.  "Precise" indicates that the main school/hostel building is within 25 metres of the point. "Approximate" indicates that the precise location of the main school building/hostel building is not known and documentation exists that describes the approximate location the school. "Predicted" indicates that location of the school/hostel building is unknown and no documentation has been found that describes where the school/hostel was located. This field was created by Morgan Hite and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

The precision in kilometres for the schools/hostel locations. 0 indicates precisely located schools/hostels;  The value indicates that the school/hostel is likely located within the specified distance of this point. For example, 0.5 indicates that the school/hostel building is likely located within 0.5 kilometres of the point. This field was created by Morgan Hite and updated by Rosa Orlandini.
The URL of the photo of the school or hostel, if available. This field can be used to display a thumbnail image of a school. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

The title of the photo of the residential school or hostel. The photos are primarily of the school/hostel buildings or aerial views of the school/hostel sites. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.
The attributed source of the photo. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.

The status of the main school building or hostel at that location. (1) "Present" = Building is still standing as of 2019. (2) "Not Present" = Building is not present on the site. (3) "Remains Present" = The foundations or the ruins of the main school building are present. (4) "Unconfirmed" there are multiple buildings still present on the site and/or community, and the precise main building cannot be determined. This field was created by Morgan Hite and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

The religious affiliation of the school or hostel. "Anglican" refers to schools/hostels that affiliated with the Church of England, New England Company and the Anglican Church of Canada. "Methodist" refers to schools/hostels that were affiliated with Methodist missions and churches. "Roman Catholic" refers to schools/hostels affiliated with orders and missions of the Roman Catholic Church. "Presbyterian" refers to schools/hostels that were affiliated with Presbyterian missions and churches. that were run by missions affiliated with the  Presbyterian Church of Canada. "United Church" refers to schools/hostels that were affiliated with the United Church of Canada. With the creation of the United Church in 1922, the Methodist and some Presbyterian schools became with affiliated with the United Church. "Baptist" is a school/hostel run by Baptist missionaries. "Mennonite" schools/hostels operated by Mennonite missionaries. "Non-Denominational" are federally run residential schools and hostels with no religious affiliation. This field was created by the NCTR and adapted by Rosa Orlandini.
Name of the municipality that the school was located. In rural and remote areas, the nearest municipality is listed. This field was created by NCTR and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

The Indigenous name (if known) of the municipality and/or reserve that the school/hostel is located. Information came from First Nations/Inuit community websites and federal government sources. This field was generated by Rosa Orlandini.
The former name of the reserve and/or municipality. Information came from archival and federal government sources. This field was generated by Rosa Orlandini.
The name of the province or territory where the school/hostel is located. This field is based upon the contemporary boundaries of the Provinces and Territories. This field was generated by the NCTR.

Specifies if the geographic coordinates of the school/hostel location in this database is different from the coordinates originally supplied by NCTR. (1) "Same" coordinates are the same as the NCTR coordinates (2) "New"  school location is a new location. The location didn't appear in the original NCTR dataset. (3) "Moved" the school location in the NCTR dataset has been moved to a more accurate location. If it moved 100 metres or more, then the distance is noted. This field was created by Rosa Orlandini.
